skill.name: dev-servers
skill.description: Start local FastAPI and Vite development servers after checking dependencies and required backend environment setup.
skill.summary: Starts backend and frontend development servers for a local full-stack app.
skill.author: AppleLamps

security_audit.summary: The skill is a short local development helper with Bash access for dependency checks, dependency installation, and server startup. Most high-severity secret findings are false positives because the text asks only to verify key setup and explicitly forbids exposing the key, but the install and server commands still execute project code.

remediation.issue: Dependency installation executes third-party package code.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for explicit user approval before running install commands and show which manifest will be used.

remediation.issue: Server startup executes local project code and npm scripts.
remediation.suggestion: Confirm the target directories and commands before launch, then report only process status and local ports.

remediation.issue: Environment checks mention a sensitive API key.
remediation.suggestion: Check only whether the key name is present and never display, copy, or log the value.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 11 only names the backend virtual environment directory in documentation. It is not a shell execution instruction or dynamic command.
Line 12 only names the frontend dependency directory in documentation. The backticks format a path and do not execute code.
Line 15 instructs the agent to run pip install in the backend directory. Installing dependencies can execute package build hooks and changes the local environment.
Line 16 instructs the agent to run npm install in the frontend directory. npm installs can execute lifecycle scripts from project dependencies.
Line 19 starts uvicorn against local application code. This is expected for the skill, but it still executes project code through Bash.
Line 20 starts the frontend through npm run dev. This executes the project script defined by the repository and should be treated as command execution.
Line 22 formats .env and OPENAI_API_KEY as inline text. It asks for a configuration check and does not contain a shell command.
The URL on line 19 is localhost for the backend development server. It is not an external network destination or exfiltration endpoint.
The URL on line 20 is localhost for the frontend development server. It documents a local port and does not send data to a remote service.
Line 22 asks to verify that OPENAI_API_KEY is configured, not to print or transmit its value. The guardrail on line 30 further says never to expose or log it.
Line 30 is a protective guardrail that forbids exposing or logging OPENAI_API_KEY. It reduces secret-handling risk rather than creating it.
Line 22 references checking that an environment file and key setting exist, not reading secret values. This is bounded by the instruction to never expose or log the key.

content.value_statement: Running a full-stack app locally often requires several checks and commands. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through backend and frontend startup.
actual_capabilities: Checks for a backend virtual environment before startup.
Checks for frontend dependencies before startup.
Suggests backend dependency installation when requirements are missing.
Suggests frontend dependency installation when packages are missing.
Starts FastAPI through uvicorn on a local port.
Starts the Vite frontend on a local port.
limitations: Assumes backend and frontend directories match the documented layout.
Requires user approval before dependency installation.
Does not configure production hosting or deployment.
Does not validate application code correctness.

use_cases.title: Start a Local App
use_cases.description: Bring up the backend and frontend during daily development.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Review Environment
use_cases.description: Launch the app locally before testing a feature branch.

use_cases.title: Onboard to a Project
use_cases.description: Check required dependencies and environment setup before first local launch.

prompt_templates.title: Start the App
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the backend and frontend development servers for this project.

prompt_templates.title: Check Dependencies First
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether backend and frontend dependencies are installed, then ask before installing anything missing.

prompt_templates.title: Launch and Report Ports
prompt_templates.prompt: Start both local development servers and report the backend and frontend ports when they are ready.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Port Conflicts
prompt_templates.prompt: Start the local app, warn me about port conflicts, and suggest the safest next action if a port is busy.

output_examples.output: The assistant checks dependency folders, asks before installing missing packages, starts both services, and reports the local server addresses.

output_examples.input: Run the servers and watch for setup issues.
output_examples.output: The assistant verifies environment setup, avoids showing secret values, warns about busy ports, and summarizes which services started successfully.

best_practices: Confirm dependency installation before running package managers.
Keep secret values hidden when checking environment setup.
Stop unused local servers before starting new sessions.
anti_patterns: Running install commands without user approval.
Printing API keys or environment file contents.
Assuming the documented ports are always available.

faq.question: What does this skill start?
faq.answer: It starts a FastAPI backend and a Vite frontend for local development.

faq.question: Does it install dependencies automatically?
faq.answer: It should ask for user approval before installing backend or frontend dependencies.

faq.question: Does it expose API keys?
faq.answer: No. The skill says the API key must never be exposed or logged.

faq.question: Which ports does it expect?
faq.answer: It documents backend port 8000 and frontend port 5173 for local use.

faq.question: Can it deploy the app?
faq.answer: No. It is focused on local development server startup only.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.
